classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the SSA ambiguous case, retain and validate both supplementary angles, then use the angle sum and sine rule to complete both triangles.

content.prompt: Determine the possible dimensions for triangle $ABC$ given $AB=5.3\text{ cm}$, $\angle BAC=33^\circ$ and $BC=3.4\text{ cm}$. Give the remaining side length to 1 decimal place and the remaining angles to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin C}{5.3}&=\frac{\sin33^\circ}{3.4}\\\sin C&=\frac{5.3\sin33^\circ}{3.4}\\C_1&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{5.3\sin33^\circ}{3.4}\right)\\C_1&\approx58^\circ6'\\C_2&=180^\circ-C_1\\C_2&\approx121^\circ54'.\end{align*}$$
Both values give $33^\circ+C<180^\circ$, so both are valid. Retain unrounded angles in the side calculations.

First triangle:
$$\begin{align*}B_1&=180^\circ-33^\circ-C_1\\B_1&\approx88^\circ54'\\\frac{AC_1}{\sin B_1}&=\frac{3.4}{\sin33^\circ}\\AC_1&=\frac{3.4\sin B_1}{\sin33^\circ}\\AC_1&\approx6.2\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Second triangle:
$$\begin{align*}B_2&=180^\circ-33^\circ-C_2\\B_2&\approx25^\circ6'\\\frac{AC_2}{\sin B_2}&=\frac{3.4}{\sin33^\circ}\\AC_2&=\frac{3.4\sin B_2}{\sin33^\circ}\\AC_2&\approx2.6\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
